qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2130-04-19 to 2130-05-03, what combined features made acute coronary syndrome less likely than a non-cardiac cause for the initial chest pain?
qas.answer: Pleuritic pain, normal EKG, non-dynamic troponins; CT ruled PE/aorta.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2130-04-19 to 2130-05-03, how did the doctor interpret an elevated troponin in the context of dialysis when assessing for heart attack?
qas.answer: Likely baseline elevation in dialysis; no concerning rise/other marker flat.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2130-04-19 to 2130-05-03, why did the team choose omeprazole rather than continuing Maalox-type antacids for symptom control?
qas.answer: Kidney failure limits aluminum antacids; PPI treats suspected gastritis/irritation.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2130-04-19 to 2130-05-03, what diagnostic sequence was used to evaluate painful swallowing, and what did each step show?
qas.answer: Barium swallow negative; then endoscopy showed gastritis/duodenitis.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2130-04-19 to 2130-05-03, what was the leading suspected source of the bloodstream infection and what evidence supported it?
qas.answer: Dialysis catheter source; coagulase-negative staph in blood cultures.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2130-04-19 to 2130-05-03, what clinical change prompted catheter removal and a “line holiday” despite appropriate antibiotic coverage?
qas.answer: Persistent fevers on vancomycin suggested ongoing line source.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2130-04-19 to 2130-05-03, what was the patient’s main fear about removing the dialysis line, and how did the team address it?
qas.answer: Fear no new access after failed fistulas; IR involved to secure temporary access.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2130-04-19 to 2130-05-03, why did Infectious Disease recommend restarting both Bactrim and azithromycin prophylaxis?
qas.answer: Very low CD4 with prior PCP; needs PCP and MAC prophylaxis.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2130-04-19 to 2130-05-03, what events led from failed neck catheter placement attempts to choosing a femoral tunneled catheter?
qas.answer: Venogram showed central venous occlusions; neck access unsafe, so femoral tunneled line planned/placed.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2130-04-19 to 2130-05-03, how did serial chest X-ray findings influence the decision to start and then stop cefepime?
qas.answer: New retrocardiac opacity + fever prompted cefepime; opacity resolved and afebrile so stopped.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2130-04-19 to 2130-05-03, why was vancomycin continued even after repeat blood cultures were negative?
qas.answer: To complete planned course for prior catheter-associated bacteremia.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2130-04-19 to 2130-05-03, what medication interaction concern could require changing the patient’s acid-suppression therapy when antiretroviral therapy is restarted?
qas.answer: Omeprazole can interact with some ART; may switch to ranitidine.
